title: HTTPS, Content Security Policy (CSP) and security headers

videos.script:
A padlock in the address bar says the connection is private. {{padlock}} It says nothing about what came down it.

So this lesson has two halves. {{https}} First what HTTPS gives, and the one header that keeps a site on it.

Then the headers that tell the browser what a page may do. {{csp}} The most important is the Content Security Policy. It lists where scripts, styles and images may come from. Anything else, the browser refuses.

You write a test first, against the built site. {{test}} It fails, because the site sends no headers at all. Then you add the policy, and it passes.

Then the witness. {{witness}} A tiny script that changes the page's title. On the dev server it runs. On the built site, the browser refuses it, and says why.

Last, how to roll a policy out without breaking a live site. {{report}} Report first. Enforce once the reports are quiet.
